To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
N1-induced mammary tumor cells are addicted to high cyclin D1 expression for proliferation and survival and that decreasing cyclinD1 expression would be an efficient therapy for N1-induced tumors.
N1IC-exposed mammary stem/progenitor-like cells are highly dependent on cyclin D1 and that decreasing cyclinD1 levels is an efficient treatment for N1-induced tumors.
Notch1-induced tumors are addicted to cyclinD1, and decreasing cyclinD1 levels would be a potential treatment for these tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of cyclin D in the Notch-1-induced transformation of mammary cells, and the potential use of this knowledge for the design of new therapeutic strategies.
the identification of the cell of origin of mammary tumors induced by N 1 signaling and the mechanisms by which cyclin D1 is required for their development.
the identification and characterization of mammary stem cells, their differentiation, and the role of cyclin D in their maintenance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Notch1 signaling induces mammary tumors in mice and that cyclin D1 plays a key role in tumor initiation and maintenance.
the Notch signaling pathway is a major player in mammary stem cell self-renewal, and the Notch1/cyclin D1 axis is critical to the development of mammary tumors in this model.
the mammary stem cells in the mouse are CD24+ CD24high and that the CD24int CD24low cells are mammosphere-formers but not stem cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyclin D1 plays a crucial role in the maintenance of the stem cell state, and its inhibition may revert N1-expressing tumor-initiating cells to a state of differentiation and lower malignancy.
the N1IC-driven expansion of mammary stem/progenitor populations is dependent on cyclin D1, and that the tumor-initiating cells generated by N1IC are addicted to cyclinD1.

the N1IC-exposed mammary cells that are addicted to cyclinD1 and are tumor-initiating are derived from bi-potential CD24+ CD 29high cells that are expanded by N1 signaling in young females and that these cells can revert to the bi-potential state after transplantation in the absence of N1IC or after knockdown of cyclinD1 in the N1IC tumor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Notch-1 signaling can induce the generation of tumor-initiating cells from mammary stem/progenitor cell subsets.
the N1IC-induced mammary tumors are not self-sustained, but rather require the presence of normal epithelial cells to maintain their malignancy.
Notch signaling can be a double-edged sword.
